title: susi-core off the async runtime and the HTTP stack
goal: Cut the cold `cargo build -p susi` critical path by taking susi-core off tokio, hyper, h2, mio and ureq. The peer MCP client's transport becomes a std::net HTTP/1.1 module inside susi-core (plain http:// only, https refused by name, one total budget, Content-Length/chunked/until-close bodies, redirects never followed, the security behaviour of mcp_client unchanged: attested credentials, no bearer off-host, sealed bodies). Provider futures become runtime-agnostic (core's run_blocking thread future and block_on), so the owner-side provider dispatch needs no runtime; the never-set async evidence task-local and the truth verifier's runtime go (cross_examine is synchronous). Callers import inference_wire from susi-adapters-llm, its real home. susi-core's normal dependencies lose susi-http-transport, susi-adapters-llm and susi-vendor-tokio.
acceptance: cargo test -p susi-core --lib plain_http --offline --locked passes: framed POST and DELETE requests, Content-Length, chunked and until-close bodies, interim 1xx skipped, error statuses returned and redirects not followed, the body cap, malformed bodies refused, one budget bounding a silent server and a stalled body, https:// and header injection refused.
